title: Ordinal analysis applied to the results of positive matrix factorization of chemical ionization mass spectrometry data
author: Kong, Pettersson
materials: units are eliminated, which allows for gas (time series) and particle phase (time series of thermograms) data to be analyzed by PMF simultaneously; (

steps.title: Collect HR‑ToF‑CIMS data
steps.instruction: Operate a high‑resolution time‑of‑flight chemical ionization mass spectrometer (HR‑ToF‑CIMS) equipped with a FIGAERO inlet, switching the inlet between gas and particle phase measurements every 45 min, record the raw signal, average the data to a 1 min time resolution, and extract peak integrals over a ±0.5 m/z span around each integer m/z from 140 to 339.

steps.title: Assemble data matrix
steps.instruction: Create a matrix where each column corresponds to a nominal mass (m/z) and each row to a 1‑minute time point, including both gas‑phase time series and particle‑phase thermogram series.

steps.title: Normalize intensities
steps.instruction: Normalize the intensities in each nominal mass to remove units and enable equal comparison of all signals; assign analytical uncertainties of approximately 5 % of the signal intensities (error proportional to signal).

steps.title: Run EPA PMF 5.0
steps.instruction: Run Positive Matrix Factorization using the open‑source program EPA PMF 5.0 on the normalized matrix and obtain Factor Profiles, Factor Contributions, Residuals, and Run Comparisons.

steps.title: Select Factor Profiles
steps.instruction: For ordinal analysis, retain only the Factor Profile (FP) results, which list the fraction of each factor for each m/z.

steps.title: Rank m/z by factor fraction
steps.instruction: For each factor, rank the m/z values in descending order of their FP fractions to identify the most influential m/z for that factor.

steps.title: Create rank maps
steps.instruction: Plot the rank (position) versus m/z for each factor to generate rank‑map visualizations; these maps can be used for cluster analysis and factor identification.

steps.title: Interpret ranked m/z
steps.instruction: Identify the most typical species in each factor from the highest‑ranked m/z; optionally consult high‑resolution mass spectra or literature to assign molecular formulas to those m/z.
